fields.name: The Wild Titan

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (4/Day or 5/Day in Lair)
trait.text: If the titan fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
trait.text: The titan has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Runic Sever
trait.text: If the titan starts its turn within 50 feet of a stone at least 10 feet high and 10 feet wide that is carved with the glyph representing its forgotten creator, the titan takes 50 necrotic damage and is poisoned until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Siege Monster
trait.text: The titan deals double damage to objects and structures.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The titan makes two Massive Fist attacks. It can replace one or both attacks with a use of Thrown Boulder.

action.name: Massive Fist
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +17 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit: 28 (4d8 + 10) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Huge or smaller creature, it is grappled (escape DC 20) from one of two fists and restrained until the grapple ends.

action.name: Thrown Boulder
action.text: The titan hurls a boulder at a point it can see within 150 feet of itself. Each creature in a 10-foot radius sphere centered on that point must make a DC 25 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 14 (4d6) bludgeoning damage and is knocked prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

action.name: Wild Roar (Recharge 5-6)
action.text: Each of the titan's enemies with 100 feet of it must succeed on a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw or be charmed until the start of the titan's next turn. While charmed in this way, the creature must use its action to make its most powerful melee or ranged attacks against the nearest creature it can see.

legendary.name: Legendary Action (3/Turn, 4/Turn in Lair)
legendary.text: The titan can take 3 legendary actions (4 in Lair), choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The titan regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

legendary.name: Arm Sweep
legendary.text: Each creature in a 20-foot cone must make a DC 25 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 9 (2d8) bludgeoning damage and is knocked prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

legendary.name: Stomping Stride
legendary.text: The titan moves up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. It can enter a Huge or smaller creature's space, and the creature is pushed to nearest unoccupied space.

legendary.name: Crushing Hurl (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary.text: The titan hurls an object it is holding, a creature it is grappling, or a Large clod of earth to a space within 100 feet. Each creature in the projectile's space, including a hurled creature, must make a DC 25 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 19 (2d8 + 10) bludgeoning damage and is knocked prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

legendary.name: The Wild Titan's Lair
legendary.text: The Wild Titan's lair is a hollowed-out peak in the mountain range the creature stalks. If encountered in its lair, the Wild Titan has a challenge rating of 22 (41,000 XP).

legendary.name: Regional Effects
legendary.text:
The region containing the Wild Titan's lair is changed by its presence, creating the following effects:

	Whiteout. Within 1 mile of the lair, there is a 75 percent chance every day of heavy precipitation.

	Wild Hunger. Within 1 mile of the lair, creatures always feel ravenously hungry, no matter how much they've eaten. A creature that finishes a long rest in this area must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or gain 1 level of exhaustion. A creature that doesn't require food succeeds automatically.

If the Wild Titan dies or moves its lair elsewhere, these effects end immediately.

fields.description:
Ferocious Giant of the Wilderness

Wandering the most inhospitable mountain ranges, the Wild Titan is the wilderness made manifest, created long ago by a forgotten will for a purpose that none know. Favoring solitude in the most remote places of the world, when it encounters settlements and "civilized" people, it wants only to turn them to primal savagery or crush them beneath its immense bulk.

	Secret. The name of the Wild Titan's forgotten creator is its undoing. Recovering the lost name and carving its glyph form into a stone creates a zone that severs the titan's connection to the wild.

Source:	The Crooked Moon p. 578 (Third Party)

fields.name: Corn Dolly
fields.languages: understands Common but doesn't speak it

trait.name: Husk Body
trait.text: The corn dolly can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.

trait.name: Uneasy Visage
trait.text: The strange, childlike inked face unnerves onlookers. While a creature is holding the corn dolly, creatures within 10 feet of it have disadvantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks made against the creature.

trait.name: Find Familiar
trait.text: With the DM's permission, a character who casts the 'Find Familiar' spell can choose to summon a Corn Dolly.

action.name: Husk Cut
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 1 slashing damage plus 4 (1d8) psychic damage.

action.name: Blank Stare
action.text: The corn dolly stares at one creature it can see within 30 feet of itself. The target must make a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw, taking 10 (3d6) psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

action.name: Sowing Dread (2/Day)
action.text: The corn dolly radiates dread in a 15-foot cone. Each creature of the corn dolly's choice in that area must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened until the end of its next turn.

reaction.name: Silent Protector
reaction.text: When a creature within 60 feet of the corn dolly fails a saving throw against an effect that doesn't deal damage, the corn dolly suffers the effects of the failure instead of the creature.

fields.description:
Grain Husk Companion (Curved blade plated in gold)

Crafted from dried husks and bound with twine, corn dollies' delicate forms are stitched together with rustic care. Their faces are ink-brushed with simple, childlike expressions—smiling mouths that curve a bit too wide and hollow eyes that seem to stare far beyond the physical world. The Constructs are spirits of deceased Humanoids drawn to the hollow corn husk shell, seeking refuge. These spirits retain faint traces of who they once were—a protective instinct entwined with a simmering fury. Once animated, the dolls reflect this dual nature: acting as silent guardians one moment and vengeful specters the next.

Source:	The Crooked Moon p. 581 (Third Party)

fields.name: Crooked Hare
fields.skill: Deception +5, History +2, Sleight of Hand +5, Stealth +5

trait.name: Trackless Step
trait.text: The crooked hare leaves no tracks, or it leaves the tracks of a Large or smaller creature of its choice. If it isn't incapacitated, it can share the effects of this trait with another creature within 5 feet of itself (no action required).

trait.name: Find Familiar
trait.text: With the DM's permission, a character who casts the 'Find Familiar' spell can choose to summon a Crooked Hare.

action.name: Twisting Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage, and if the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 11 Charisma saving throw or become cursed for 24 hours. The cursed creature's limbs sporadically twist and move in unnatural ways, giving the creature disadvantage on attack rolls and on ability checks that rely on Charisma.

fields.description:
Crooked Trickster (Anything stolen or gained by trickery)

Crooked hares look like rabbits at first glance, but their true nature is given away by the antlers and wings they grow and the cunning gleam in their eyes. They are mischievous tricksters that delight in stealing things from unsuspecting travelers and hiding them in amusing, slightly dangerous, or just unlikely places. If roused to anger or cornered, crooked hares deliver a bite that carries an unsettling—if minor—curse. Despite their troublesome nature, crooked hares might serve as companions for woods-crafty folk who have a good sense of humor.

Source:	The Crooked Moon p. 582 (Third Party)

fields.name: Devil's Glove

trait.name: Scent of Death
trait.text: Creatures that can smell have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks made to find the devil's glove.

trait.name: Spider Climb
trait.text: The devil's glove can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

trait.name: Find Familiar
trait.text: With the DM's permission, a character who casts the 'Find Familiar' spell can choose to summon a Devil's Glove.

action.name: Tendril
action.text:
Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (2d6) necrotic damage, and the devil's glove attaches to the target. While attached, the devil's glove can't make Tendril attacks against other targets, and if the target is a creature, the target is poisoned until the start of its next turn if it can smell the devil's glove.
	The devil's glove can detach itself by spending 5 feet of its movement. The target or a creature within 5 feet of it can detach the devil's glove as an action.

action.name: Decaying Bloom (2/Day)
action.text: The devil's glove releases a cloud of spores. Each creature within 10 feet of the devil's glove must make a DC 12 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 9 (2d8) necrotic damage and can't regain hit points until the start of the devil's glove's next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

action.name: Symbiosis (Bonus Action)
action.text: The devil's glove forms a magical bond with a willing creature it touches. The bonded creature doesn't need to eat or drink, and the creature has advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the poisoned condition. The bond ends when the devil's glove dies, the creature dies, the devil's glove ends the bond (no action required), or the devil's glove uses this bonus action again.

fields.description:
Five-Fingered Fungus (Rare wood chips)

Comprised of five twitching, blood-red tendrils lined with black slime, the devil's glove fungus feeds voraciously of decaying matter, unwary insects, and small creatures. Resembling a long-fngered hand, they grow from bulbous roots that look like leathery, white eggs and constantly emit an overpowering scent of death and rot. Despite their unpleasant aura, these fungus creatures can form beneficial relationships with others, providing nourishment and resilience in exchange for protection and a ready supply of decaying material to feed upon.

Source:	The Crooked Moon p. 583 (Third Party)

fields.name: Dingpot

trait.name: Boil and Bubble
trait.text: While the dingpot isn't incapacitated, it can provide enough heat to boil water within its vessel.

trait.name: Find Familiar
trait.text: With the DM's permission, a character who casts the 'Find Familiar' spell can choose to summon a Dingpot.

action.name: Steam Spray
action.text: Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) fire damage, and the target has disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the start of the dingpot's next turn. Being underwater doesn't grant resistance to this fire damage.

action.name: Brew (1/Day)
action.text:
The dingpot produces a magical elixir within its vessel. The elixir remains potent for 24 hours. It can choose from the following brews:

	Healing Draught. As a bonus action, a creature can drink the elixir to regain 4 (1d6 + 1) hit points.

	Lucky Draught. As a bonus action, a creature can drink the elixir to gain startling luck for 10 minutes. When the creature fails an ability check or a saving throw, it can reroll the d20 and use the new roll. Once this causes a roll to succeed, the effects of the elixir end early.

fields.description:
Jovial Cauldron Helper (Spices and rose quartz)

Dingpots are animated objects created to assist in magical and alchemical research—or simply to help in the kitchen. Often cheerful, dingpots delight in serving up delicious meals, soothing tea, and the occasional magical draught.

Source:	The Crooked Moon p. 584 (Third Party)

fields.name: Ghost Crawler

trait.name: Ephemeral Body
trait.text: The crawler can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.

trait.name: Seer's Strand
trait.text: The crawler can see and hear through the space of its Ether Webs as if it were in that space.

trait.name: Spider Climb
trait.text: The crawler can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

trait.name: Web Sense
trait.text: While in contact with a web, the crawler knows the exact location of any other creature in contact with the same web.

trait.name: Web Walker
trait.text: The crawler ignores movement restrictions caused by webbing.

trait.name: Find Familiar
trait.text: With the DM's permission, a character who casts the 'Find Familiar' spell can choose to summon a Ghost Crawler.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The crawler makes two Bite attacks.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage, and if the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned until the start of the crawler's next turn.

action.name: Ether Webs (2/Day)
action.text: The crawler fills a 5-foot cube with invisible, ephemeral webs for 8 hours. If the web isn't anchored between two solid masses (such as walls or trees) or layered across a floor, wall, or ceiling, the web collapses on itself and vanishes. When a creature touches the webbing, the crawler knows the location of the creature as long as they are on the same plane of existence.

fields.description:
Spirit Spider (Silk threads soaked in wine)

Silent and nearly invisible, ghost crawlers skitter between the darkest corners, hiding and watching. Their diminutive, ghostly, spider-like bodies are ill-defned and as translucent as a wisp of smoke, while their legs are long, uneven, and jarringly solid. The webs they spin are ephemeral and ghastly, allowing the crawlers to sense through them regardless of the distance.

Source:	The Crooked Moon p. 585 (Third Party)

fields.name: Goatstealer

trait.name: Pack Tactics
trait.text: The goatstealer has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the goatstealer's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

trait.name: Stench
trait.text: Any creature that starts its turn within 5 feet of the goatstealer must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned until the start of its next turn. On a successful save, the creature is immune to the Stench of all goatstealers for 1 hour.

trait.name: Find Familiar
trait.text: With the DM's permission, a character who casts the 'Find Familiar' spell can choose to summon a Goatstealer.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) poison damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it is grappled (escape DC 12). Until the grapple ends, at the start of each of the goatstealer's turns, the target takes 3 (1d6) poison damage.

fields.description:
Hungry Livestock Snatcher (Incense and spoiled meat)

The hairless, reeking goatstealers are vicious predators and scavengers that earn their name from their habit of preying upon livestock. They latch onto prey with wicked, needle-like teeth, delivering lethal venom and devouring creatures far larger than its wiry frame would suggest is possible. Especially dangerous in packs, the carrion-yet-peaty stench of goatstealers is the stuf of legend.

Source:	The Crooked Moon p. 586 (Third Party)

fields.name: Hemonculus
fields.resist: cold, fire

trait.name: Blood Sense
trait.text: The hemonculus knows the location of any creature within 60 feet of it that has half its hit points or fewer, unless the creature is a Construct or Undead.

trait.name: Flyby
trait.text: The hemonculus doesn't provoke an opportunity attack when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
trait.text: The hemonculus has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Find Familiar
trait.text: With the DM's permission, a character who casts the 'Find Familiar' spell can choose to summon a Hemonculus.

action.name: Claw
action.text:
Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) necrotic damage, and the hemonculus attaches to the target. While attached, the hemonculus automatically hits the target with its Claw attacks.
	The hemonculus can detach itself by spending 5 feet of its movement. The target or a creature within 5 feet of it can detach the hemonculus as an action.

action.name: Exsanguinate (1/Day)
action.text:
The hemonculus magically draws blood from nearby creatures. Each creature of the hemonculus' choice within 15 feet of the hemonculus must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 10 (3d6) necrotic damage, and it can't regain hit points until the start of the hemonculus's next turn. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage only.
	If the hemonculus is attached to a creature, the hemonculus regains hit points equal to the necrotic damage taken by that target.

fields.description:
Sanguine Servitor (Fresh blood and gem dust)

Hemonculus are servitors created by a blood magic ritual that binds a fiendish spirit into a blood-formed body. For the cost of a small sacrifce in blood (the creator's own or otherwise), the creatures serve as spies and assist in procuring further blood for magical use.

Source:	The Crooked Moon p. 587 (Third Party)

fields.name: Magpie of Omens

trait.name: Flyby
trait.text: The magpie doesn't provoke an opportunity attack when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

trait.name: Find Familiar
trait.text: With the DM's permission, a character who casts the 'Find Familiar' spell can choose to summon a Magpie of Omens.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The magpie makes two Beak attacks.

action.name: Beak
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d4 + 3) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) radiant damage.

action.name: Bonded Voice (Bonus Action)
action.text: The magpie can form or dissolve a magical bond with a willing creature within 5 feet. While the bond lasts, the bonded creature can speak through the magpie using the creature's own voice and language, but with a birdlike lilt. The bond ends when the creature dies or if the magpie creates a new bond.

reaction.name: One for Sorrow (1/Day)
reaction.text: When a creature within 30 feet of the magpie makes an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw with advantage, the target rolls 1d6 and subtracts it from the total.

reaction.name: Two for Joy (2/Day)
reaction.text: When the magpie or another creature within 30 feet of it makes an ability check or a saving throw, the target rolls 1d4 and adds it to the total

fields.description:
Bird of Fate and Fortune (Crystal or gemstone shards)

To those who respect the Old Ways, this bird of black and white brings tidings both fair and foul. Although the omens the magpie delivers can bring joy and grief in equal measure, they are always trustworthy.

Source:	The Crooked Moon p. 588 (Third Party)

fields.name: Moonshine
fields.resist: acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, thunder; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks
fields.conditionImmune: exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrifed, poisoned, prone, restrained, unconscious

trait.name: Detect Life
trait.text: The moonshine magically senses the direction of creatures up to 60 feet away that aren't Constructs or Undead.

trait.name: Ephemeral
trait.text: The moonshine can't wear or carry anything.

trait.name: Illumination
trait.text: The moonshine sheds bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light for an additional 15 feet.

trait.name: Incorporeal Movement
trait.text: The moonshine can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

trait.name: Find Familiar
trait.text: With the DM's permission, a character who casts the 'Find Familiar' spell can choose to summon a Moonshine.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The moonshine makes two Gloomy Touch attacks.

action.name: Gloomy Touch
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) psychic damage.

action.name: Siphon Life (2/Day)
action.text: The moonshine magically targets a creature that isn't a Construct or Undead that it can see within 5 feet of itself. The target must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of the moonshine's next turn, and the moonshine or a creature of its choice within 30 feet of it regains 3 (1d6) hit points.

fields.description:
Lingering Soul Guide (Broken glass and powdered onyx)

When a person dies with unfinished business, their soul can remain shackled to the living world as an Undead spirit. Usually such spirits rest and move on when their business is concluded, but some remain as companions, guides, and helpers for the living. Moonshines are spirits who resolved their emotional tethers but have chosen to linger on. They often take a liking to a living person and choose to help them through their life's journey.

Source:	The Crooked Moon p. 589 (Third Party)

fields.name: Nameless Thing

trait.name: Flyby
trait.text: The nameless thing doesn't provoke an opportunity attack when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

trait.name: Find Familiar
trait.text: With the DM's permission, a character who casts the 'Find Familiar' spell can choose to summon a Nameless Thing.

action.name: Psychic Strike
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d12 + 3) psychic damage, and if the target is a creature, it is frightened until the start of the nameless thing's next turn.

action.name: Invisibility
action.text:
The nameless thing casts Invisibility on itself, requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability.
	When it casts the spell, the nameless thing can extend the effect of the spell to a creature it is touching. The spell ends early if either creature breaks the spell on itself or if the nameless thing stops touching the other creature. Once the nameless thing extends the spell in this way, it can't do so again until it finishes a long rest.

fields.spells: Invisibility
fields.description:
Unknowable Lifeform from Beyond (Meteorite fragments)

Nameless things are alien minds bound into physical vessels, most often diminutive animals, objects, or pieces of monsters. These creatures can creep into the world when outer infuence seeps into existence but are usually deliberately invited.

Source:	The Crooked Moon p. 590 (Third Party)

fields.name: Ravencraft

trait.name: Undead Fortitude
trait.text: If damage reduces the ravencraft to 0 hit points, it makes a Constitution saving throw (DC 5 plus the damage taken) unless the damage is radiant or from a critical hit. On a successful save, the ravencraft drops to 1 hit point instead.

trait.name: Find Familiar
trait.text: With the DM's permission, a character who casts the 'Find Familiar' spell can choose to summon a Ravencraft.

action.name: Beak
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) necrotic damage.

action.name: Harbinger of Doom (2/Day)
action.text: The ravencraft lets out a wail of anguish commingling with the croaking of ravens. One creature within 60 feet of it must make a DC 11 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 5 (1d10) psychic damage, and it is frightened until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

reaction.name: Death Veil
reaction.text: When a creature within 30 feet of the ravencraft makes a death saving throw, the creature has advantage on the save.

fields.description:
Undead Avian Amalgamation (Silver wire)

Ravencrafts are a grotesque fusion of feathers, sinew, and bone. Their tiny form is a contorted and twisted nightmare carelessly sewn together into the mockery of a bird. The mere presence of a ravencraft is an afront to natural death and can keep further death at bay, or they can chill the hearts of their foes with cries of torment from beyond the grave.

Source:	The Crooked Moon p. 591 (Third Party)

fields.name: Salmon of Knowledge
fields.speed: 5 ft., fy 30 ft. (hover; Orb of Water only), swim 30 ft.
fields.languages: understands all but can't speak, Telepathy 60 ft.
fields.resist: fire (Orb of Water only), psychic

trait.name: Orb of Water
trait.text: The salmon is surrounded by a sphere of flowing water that moves with it. While inside of the sphere, the salmon has resistance to fire damage. A creature that grapples the salmon can choose to pull it out of the orb of water. The orb of water moves up to 20 feet toward the salmon at the start of each of the salmon's turns. If it enters the salmon's space, the grapple ends on the salmon.

trait.name: Water Breathing
trait.text: The salmon can breathe only underwater.

trait.name: Find Familiar
trait.text: With the DM's permission, a character who casts the 'Find Familiar' spell can choose to summon a Salmon of Knowledge.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The salmon makes two Water Spray attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Prophetic Guidance.

action.name: Water Spray
action.text: Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) cold damage.

action.name: Prophetic Guidance (2/Day)
action.text: A creature the salmon can see within 30 feet gains a flash of foresight. Once in the next minute, when the creature fails an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw, it can roll 1d4 and add it to the total, potentially turning the failure into a success.

reaction.name: Echo from the Current
reaction.text: When a creature within 5 feet of the salmon makes an Intelligence or Wisdom check, the creature can use the salmon's Wisdom modifier (+4) in place of its own ability modifier for the check.

fields.description:
Elemental Font of Wisdom (Crushed opal)

Legends speak of the salmon of knowledge—shimmering fish said to embody the wisdom of the ages. Their scales gleam with an iridescent light, and they are forever enveloped in a sphere of gently fowing water that defes gravity. This magical orb is said to carry the essence of the sacred Current of Wisdom—where knowledge of all time and space fows through the rivers of the cosmos.

Source:	The Crooked Moon p. 592 (Third Party)
fields.environment:
coastal, planar (elemental plane of 
water), underwater

fields.name: Witchwoven

trait.name: Find Familiar
trait.text: With the DM's permission, a character who casts the 'Find Familiar' spell can choose to summon a Witchwoven.

action.name: Cursed Scratch
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage plus 3 (1d6) necrotic damage, and if the target is a creature, it has disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of the witchwoven's next turn.

reaction.name: Protective Bond
reaction.text: When a creature the witchwoven can see within 60 feet of it takes damage, the creature gains resistance to the triggering damage, and the witchwoven takes 10 (3d6) force damage.

fields.description:
Helper Made of Twine and Twigs (Ruby wrapped in a wicker cage)

Witchwoven are little dolls or efgies made of sticks, twine, and other simple materials, then imbued with life. Some happen naturally in places sufused with old nature magic, but most are created to serve as familiars by spellcasters knowledgeable in the Old Ways.

Source:	The Crooked Moon p. 593 (Third Party)

fields.name: Grim
fields.conditionImmune: frightened, grappled, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained

trait.name: Proficiency Bonus
trait.text: equals your proficiency bonus

trait.name: Armor Class
trait.text: 13 plus your Wisdom modifier.

trait.name: Hit Points
trait.text: 5 plus five times your ranger level (the grim has a number of Hit Dice [d8s] equal to your ranger level)

trait.name: Incorporeal Movement
trait.text: The grim can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. The grim takes 1d10 force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

trait.name: Shared Fate
trait.text: Add your proficiency bonus to any ability check or saving throw the grim makes.

action.name: Ominous Rend
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 1d6 + 3 plus your Wisdom modifier necrotic damage, and if the target is a creature, it is frightened until the start of your next turn.

reaction.name: Baleful Howl
reaction.text: When a creature moves out of the grim's reach, the target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or its speed is 0 until the end of the turn.

fields.description: Source:	The Crooked Moon p. 85 (Third Party)

fields.name: Archon of Redemption
fields.resist: radiant; bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks

trait.name: Angelic Weapons
trait.text: The archon's weapon attacks are magical. When the archon hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 3d8 radiant damage (included in the attack).

trait.name: Axiomatic Mind
trait.text: The archon can't be compelled to act in a manner contrary to its nature or its understanding of justice.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
trait.text: The archon has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: One Being

trait.name: False Appearance
trait.text: While the creepy doll remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from an ordinary, inanimate doll.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The creepy doll makes one attack with its scissors and uses Psychic Assault.

action.name: Scissors
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) slashing damage.

action.name: Psychic Assault
action.text: The creepy doll targets one creature it can see within 10 feet of it that has a brain. The target must succeed on a DC 12 Intelligence saving throw or take 11 (2d10) psychic damage. Also on a failure, roll 3d6. If the total equals or exceeds the target's Intelligence score, that score is reduced to 0. The target is stunned until it regains at least one point of Intelligence, as from the greater restoration spell or similar magic.

action.name: Body Exchange
action.text:
The creepy doll initiates an Intelligence contest with an incapacitated humanoid within 5 feet of it. If it wins the contest, the creepy doll's spirit inhabits the target's body while the target's spirit is placed into the creepy doll's body. The creepy doll controls the target's body completely. It retains its alignment, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and immunity to being charmed and frightened. It otherwise uses the possessed target's statistics, but doesn't gain access to the target's knowledge, class features, or proficiencies. The target retains its alignment, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma while inhabiting the creepy doll's body.

The body exchange lasts until the doll's spirit is forced out by magic. (The dispel evil and good spell will accomplish this, though the doll is not one of the creature types whose possession that spell normally ends.) The body and the doll must be within 5 feet of each other for such an effect to work. The target is immune to this doll's Body Exchange for 24 hours after winning the Intelligence contest or after the exchange ends.

fields.languages: any languages it knew in life
fields.resist: acid, fire, lightning, thunder, bludgeoning

trait.name: Ethereal Sight
trait.text:
The geist can see 60 feet into the Ethereal Plane when
it is on the Material Plane, and vice versa.

trait.name: Incorporeal Movement
trait.text:
The geist can move through other creatures
and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force
damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

trait.name: Geist Powers
trait.text: Geists are as varied as the humans they were in life. In addition to the traits and actions all geists possess, an individual geist might have any of the following special characteristics.

trait.name: Geist Powers: Intangible Virtue
trait.text: A living creature possessed by a white-aligned geist gains immunity to the charmed and frightened conditions, and resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. While the creature is possessed, the geist can allow it to take control of its body, but the geist can regain control at any time (no action required).

trait.name: Geist Powers: Horrifying Visage
trait.text: Black-aligned geists can make themselves terrible to behold, even when they are possessing the living. Each non-undead creature within 60 feet of the geist that can see it must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened for 1 minute. If the save fails by 5 or more, the target also ages 1d4 × 10 years. A frightened target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the frightened condition on itself on a success. If a target's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the target is immune to this geist's Horrifying Visage for the next 24 hours. The aging effect can be reversed with a greater restoration spell, but only within 24 hours of it occurring.

action.name: Withering Touch
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target 17 (4d6 + 3) necrotic damage.

action.name: Etherealness
action.text: The geist enters the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane, or vice versa. It is visible on the Material Plane while it is in the Border Ethereal, and vice versa, yet it can't affect or be affected by anything on the other plane.

action.name: Possession (Recharge 6)
action.text: One creature that the geist can see within 5 feet of it must succeed on a DC 13 Charisma saving throw or be possessed by the geist; the geist then disappears, and the target is incapacitated and loses control of its body. The geist now controls the body but doesn't deprive the target of awareness. The geist can't be targeted by any attack, spell, or other effect, except ones that turn undead, and it retains its alignment, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and immunity to being charmed and frightened. It otherwise uses the possessed target's statistics, but doesn't gain access to the target's knowledge, class features, or proficiencies. The possession lasts until the body drops to 0 hit points, the geist ends it as a bonus action, or the geist is turned or forced out by an effect like the dispel evil and good spell. When the possession ends, the geist reappears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the body. The target is immune to this geist's Possession for 24 hours after succeeding on the saving throw or after the possession ends. The geist can instead target the corpse of a creature, effectively using its own life force to animate the corpse as a zombie. The animated corpse uses zombie statistics and returns to death if the geist ends the possession.

trait.name: Berserk
trait.text:
Whenever the golem starts its turn with 40 hit points or fewer, roll a d6. On a 6, the golem goes berserk. On each of its turns while berserk, the golem attacks the nearest creature it can see. If no creature is near enough to move to and attack, the golem attacks an object, with preference for an object smaller than itself. Once the golem goes berserk, it continues to do so until it is destroyed or regains all its hit points.

The golem's creator, if within 60 feet of the berserk golem, can try to calm it by speaking firmly and persuasively. The golem must be able to hear its creator, who must take an action to make a DC 15 Charisma (Persuasion) check. If the check succeeds, the golem ceases being berserk. If it takes damage while still at 40 hit points or fewer, the golem might go berserk again.

trait.name: Aversion of Fire
trait.text: If the golem takes fire damage, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn.

trait.name: Immutable Form
trait.text: The golem is immune to any spell or effect that would alter its form.

trait.name: Lightning Absorption
trait.text: Whenever the golem is subjected to lightning damage, it takes no damage and instead regains a number of hit points equal to the lightning damage dealt.

trait.name: Magic Resistance

trait.text: The most basic skaabs are simply flesh golems, as described in the Monster Manual. But the aspiration of every skaberen is to produce a truly unique masterpiece, a goal that might see a stitcher create golems with one of the following special characteristics.

trait.name: Skaab Characteristic: Armor Plating
trait.text: Increase the skaab's Armor Class to 14 and increase its challenge rating to 6 (2,300 XP).

trait.name: Skaab Characteristic: Six Arms
trait.text: The skaab's multiattack action allows it to make three slam attacks. Increase its challenge rating to 6 (2,300 XP).

trait.name: Skaab Characteristic: Three Heads
trait.text: The skaab has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks and on saving throws against being blinded, deafened, stunned, and knocked unconscious. (Its challenge rating doesn't change.)

trait.name: Skaab Characteristic: Skaab Goliath
trait.text: This skaab has three heads, six arms, and armor plating. Increase its challenge rating to 7 (2,900 XP).

trait.name: Skaab Characteristic: Winged Skaab
trait.text: The skaab has a flying speed of 30 feet.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The vampire makes two attacks, only one of which can be a bite attack.

action.name: Claws
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) slashing damage. Instead of dealing damage, the vampire can grapple the target (escape DC 13).

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one willing creature, or a creature that is grappled by the vampire, incapacitated, or restrained. 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage plus 7 (2d6) necrotic damage. The target's hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the necrotic damage taken, and the vampire regains hit points equal to that amount. The reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its hit point maximum to 0.

action.name: Vampiric Glamer
action.text: The vampire obscures its form with mind-affecting magic that makes others perceive it as a beautiful human of the same size and shape. The illusion ends if the vampire takes a bonus action to end it or if the vampire dies. A creature that can see the vampire can take an action to visually inspect it, ending the mental effect on itself and seeing the vampire's true form with a successful DC 20 Wisdom (Perception) check.

action.name: Aura of Silence
action.text: The vampire shrouds itself in a cloak of silence to a radius of 2 feet. Within that radius, the effect is the same as the silence spell.

action.name: Variant: Elder Vampires
action.text:
The basic vampire statistics represent a "neonate"—a newly spawned vampire. Older vampires can learn powerful magic of many different kinds, and might have any of the following traits and abilities.

Shapechanger: The vampire has the Shapechanger trait of the vampire in the Monster Manual, as well as the shapechanger tag. Some vampires can turn into bat form, some can assume mist form, and a few can choose either form.

Charm: The vampire has the Charm action of the vampire in the Monster Manual.

Flight: The vampire has a flying speed of 30 feet.

Gorger: The vampire has advantage on melee attack rolls, but attack rolls against it have advantage.

Spellcasting: The vampire has the spellcasting abilities of a wizard or cleric.

Its statistics, other than its AC, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

trait.name: Keen Hearing and Smell

action.text:
The gremlin drains aether from an aether-powered device it can see within 5 feet of it. If the object isn't being worn or carried, the touch automatically drains aether. If the object is being worn or carried by a creature, the creature must succeed on a DC 11 Dexterity saving throw to keep it out of the gremlin's reach.

If the aether-powered device grants any bonus (to attack rolls, damage rolls, Armor Class, and so on), that bonus is reduced by 1. If the device has charges, it loses 1 charge. Otherwise, it stops functioning for 1 round. Left unhindered, a gremlin can completely destroy an aether-powered device.

If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it must succeed on a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw or be swallowed by the leviathan. A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the leviathan, and it takes 21 (6d6) acid damage at the start of each of the leviathan's turns.

If the leviathan takes 30 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside it, the leviathan must succeed on a DC 21 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which fall prone in a space within 10 feet of the leviathan. If the leviathan dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse by using 20 feet of movement, exiting prone.

action.name: Frightful Presence

A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the dragon's Frightful Presence for the next 24 hours.

action.name: Fire Breath (Recharge 5-6)
action.text: The dragon exhales fire in a 60-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 21 Dexterity saving throw, taking 63 (18d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

legendary.name: Legendary Actions (3/Turn)
legendary.text: The dragon can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The dragon regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

legendary.name: Detect
legendary.text: The dragon makes a Wisdom (Perception) check.

legendary.name: Tail Attack
legendary.text: The dragon makes a tail attack.

legendary.name: Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary.text: The dragon beats its wings. Each creature within 10 feet of the dragon must succeed on a DC 22 Dexterity saving throw or take 15 (2d6 + 8) bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone. The dragon can then fly up to half its flying speed.

legendary.name: Lair Actions
legendary.text:
On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the dragon takes a lair action to cause one of the following effects; the dragon can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

	• Magma erupts from a point on the ground the dragon can see within 120 feet of it, creating a 20-foot-high, 5-foot-radius geyser. Each creature in the geyser's area must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 21 (6d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

	• A tremor shakes the lair in a 60-foot radius around the dragon. Each creature other than the dragon on the ground in that area must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone.

	• Volcanic gases form a cloud in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on a point the dragon can see within 120 feet of it. The sphere spreads a round corners, and its area is lightly obscured. It lasts until initiative count 20 on the next round. Each creature that starts its turn in the cloud must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned until the end of its turn. While poisoned in this way, a creature is incapacitated.

legendary.name: Regional Effects
legendary.text:
The region containing a legendary red dragon's lair is warped by the dragon's magic, which creates one or more of the following effects:

	• Small earthquakes are common within 6 miles of the dragon's lair.

	• Water sources within 1 mile of the lair are supernaturally warm and tainted by sulfur.

	• Rocky fissures within 1 mile of the dragon's lair form portals to the Elemental Plane of Fire, allowing creatures of elemental fire into the world to dwell nearby.

If the dragon dies, these effects fade over the course of 1d10 days.

trait.text:

	• Cantrips (at will): sacred flame, spare the dying, thaumaturgy
	• 1st level (4 slots): command, detect evil and good, detect magic
	• 2nd level (3 slots): lesser restoration, zone of truth
	• 3rd level (3 slots): dispel magic, tongues
	• 4th level (3 slots): banishment, freedom of movement
	• 5th level (2 slots): flame strike, greater restoration
	• 6th level (1 slots): heroes' feast

action.name: Roar (3/Day)
action.text:
The sphinx emits a magical roar. Each time it roars before finishing a long rest, the roar is louder and the effect is different, as detailed below. Each creature within 500 feet of the sphinx and able to hear the roar must make a saving throw.

	• First Roar: Each creature that fails a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw is frightened for 1 minute. A frightened creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

	• Second Roar: Each creature that fails a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw is deafened and frightened for 1 minute. A frightened creature is paralyzed and can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

	• Third Roar: Each creature makes a DC 18 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 44 (8d10) thunder damage and is knocked prone. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn't knocked prone.

legendary.name: Claw Attack
legendary.text: The sphinx makes one claw attack.

legendary.name: Teleport (Costs 2 Actions)

legendary.name: Cast a Spell (Costs 3 Actions)
legendary.text: The sphinx casts a spell from its list of prepared spells, using a spell slot as normal.

legendary.name: Lair Actions
legendary.text:
On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the sphinx can take a lair action to cause one of the following magical effects; the sphinx can't use an effect again until it finishes a short or long rest:

	• The flow of time is altered such that every creature in the lair must reroll initiative. The sphinx can choose not to reroll.

	• The effects of time are altered such that every creature in the lair must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or become 1d20 years older or younger (the sphinx's choice), but never any younger than 1 year old. A greater restoration spell can restore a creature's age to normal.

	• The flow of time within the lair is altered such that everything within moves up to 10 years forward or backward (sphinx's choice). Only the sphinx is immediately aware of the time change. A wish spell can return the caster and up to seven other creatures designated by the caster to their normal time.

	• The sphinx shifts itself and up to seven other creatures it can see within in its lair to another plane of existence. Once outside its lair, the sphinx can't use lair actions, but it can return to its lair as a bonus action on its turn, taking up to seven creatures with it.

trait.name: Spellcasting

The marauder is a 10th-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save DC 17, +9 to hit with spell attacks). The marauder has the following cleric spells prepared:

	• Cantrips (at will): sacred flame, thaumaturgy
	• 1st level (4 slots): command, guiding bolt, shield of faith
	• 2nd level (3 slots): hold person, silence, spiritual weapon
	• 3rd level (3 slots): animate dead, dispel magic
	• 4th level (3 slots): divination, guardian of faith
	• 5th level (2 slots): contagion, insect plague

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The mummy can use its Dreadful Glare and makes one attack with its rotting fist.

action.name: Rotting Fist
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (3d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage plus 21 (6d6) necrotic damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or be cursed with mummy rot. The cursed target can't regain hit points, and its hit point maximum decreases by 10 (3d6) for every 24 hours that elapse. If the curse reduces the target's hit point maximum to 0, the target dies, and its body turns to dust. The curse lasts until removed by the remove curse spell or other magic.

action.name: Dreadful Glare
action.text: The marauder targets one creature it can see within 60 feet of it. If the target can see the marauder, it must succeed on a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw against this magic or become frightened until the end of the mummy's next turn. If the target fails the saving throw by 5 or more, it is also paralyzed for the same duration. A target that succeeds on the saving throw is immune to the Dreadful Glare of all mummies and marauders for the next 24 hours.

legendary.name: Legendary Actions (5/Turn)
legendary.text: The undead can take 5 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The undead regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

legendary.name: Attack
legendary.text: The marauder makes one attack with its rotting fist or uses its Dreadful Glare.

legendary.name: Blinding Dust
legendary.text: Blinding dust and sand swirls magically around the marauder. Each creature within 5 feet of the marauder must succeed on a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or be blinded until the end of the creature's next turn.

legendary.name: Blasphemous Word (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary.text: The marauder utters a blasphemous word. Each non-undead creature within 10 feet of the marauder that can hear the magical utterance must succeed on a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of the marauder's next turn.

legendary.name: Channel Negative Energy (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary.text: The marauder magically unleashes negative energy. Creatures within 60 feet of the marauder, including ones behind barriers and around corners, can't regain hit points until the end of the marauder's next turn.

legendary.name: Whirlwind of Sand (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary.text:
The marauder magically transforms into a whirlwind of sand, moves up to 60 feet, and reverts to its normal form. While in whirlwind form, the marauder is immune to all damage, and it can't be grappled, petrified, knocked prone, restrained, or stunned.

Equipment worn or carried by the marauder remain in its possession.

legendary.name: Lair Actions
legendary.text:
On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the mummy lord takes a lair action to cause one of the following effects; the mummy lord can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

	• Each undead creature in the lair can pinpoint the location of each living creature within 120 feet of it until initiative count 20 on the next round.

	• Each undead in the lair has advantage on saving throws against effects that turn undead until initiative count 20 on the next round.

	• Until initiative count 20 on the next round, any non-undead creature that tries to cast a spell of 4th level or lower in the mummy lord's lair is wracked with pain. The creature can choose another action, but if it tries to cast the spell, it must make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 1d6 necrotic damage per level of the spell, and the spell has no effect and is wasted.

legendary.name: Regional Effects
legendary.text:
A mummy lord's temple or tomb is warped in any of the following ways by the creature's dark presence:

	• Food instantly molders and water instantly evaporates when brought into the lair. Other non magical drinks are spoiled — wine turning to vinegar, for instance.

	• Divination spells cast within the lair by creatures other than the mummy lord have a 25 percent chance to provide misleading results, as determined by the DM. If a divination spell already has a chance to fail or become unreliable when cast multiple times, that chance increases by 25 percent.

	• A creature that takes treasure from the lair is cursed until the treasure is returned. The cursed target has disadvantage on all saving throws. The curse lasts until removed by a remove curse spell or other magic.

If the mummy lord is destroyed, these regional effects end immediately.

trait.name: Clockwork Encasement
trait.text:
The creature within the machine is a somewhat shapeless mass, both protected and given concrete manipulators by its armor. The clockwork armor has a variety of manipulators that the ahu-nixta can use to attack or to interact with objects outside of the armor. When the ahu-nixta is reduced to 0 hp, its clockwork armor breaks and the ahunixta exits it. Once out of its armor, the creature s pulpy mass no longer receives the benefits of the listed Damage or Condition Immunities, except for psychic and prone.

Without its clockwork armor, the ahu-nixta has the following statistics. AC 12, hp 37 (5d10 + 10), Strength 9 (-1), and all its modes of travel are reduced to 20 feet. In addition, it has no attack actions, though it can still cast its spells. The ahu-nixta s body can form eyes, mouths, and grabbing appendages. Its grabbing appendages can pick up objects and manipulate them, but the appendages can t be used for combat. The ahu-nixta s extra appendages can open and close glass-covered viewing ports in the clockwork armor, requiring no action, so it can see and interact with objects outside the armor.

The ahu-nixta can exit or enter its clockwork armor as a bonus action.

A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

action.name: Absorb Spirit (1/Day)
action.text: The ammut attempts to absorb the spirit of a dead or undead creature in its belly. The creature must succeed on a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or be absorbed by the ammut. The sammael's purpose is to destroy unholy monuments and statues. Its weapon attacks deal double damage to objects and structures.

trait.text: The arcamag can use its action to polymorph into a small object, such as a ring, wand, orb, rod, or scroll. Its statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

trait.name: False Appearance (Object Form Only)
trait.text: While motionless, the arcamag is indistinguishable from an ordinary object.

action.name: Attach
action.text:
Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature that can cast spells. The arcamag attaches to the target.

While attached, the arcamag doesn't attack. Instead, it causes a handful of changes in its spellcaster host (see Changes to the Host sidebar).

The arcamag can detach itself by spending 5 feet of its movement. A creature other than the host can use its action to detach the arcamag by succeeding on a DC 15 Strength check.

The host can use its action to detach the arcamag only after the host has expended all of its spell slots for the day, including the extra cantrips and spell slots gained from having the arcamag attached. Doing so doesn't require a Strength check. When the arcamag detaches itself or is detached from a host, the host takes 2 (1d4) psychic damage per spellcaster level.

action.name: Teleport (1/Day)
action.text: The arcamag magically teleports up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space. If it is attached to a host when it uses this action, it automatically detaches.

fields.name: Arcanaphage
fields.resist: bludgeoning, piercing, slashing

trait.name: Arcane Discharge
trait.text: When an arcanaphage dies, it explodes in a surge of partially-digested magical energy. Each creature within 5 feet per Feed score must make a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw, taking 3 (1d6) force damage per Feed score on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. For 1 minute afterward, the affected area is awash with volatile magic. A creature that starts its turn in the affected area takes 7 (2d6) force damage.

trait.name: Hunger
trait.text: Each time it feeds in combat, it regains hp equal to twice the level of the spell it ate and increases its Feed score by 1. The arcanaphage can't have a Feed score higher than 8, and its Feed score reduces by 1 each time it finishes a long rest.

trait.name: Ingest Magic
trait.text: At the start of each of the arcanaphage's turns, each creature within 30 feet of it that is currently maintaining concentration on a spell must make a DC 14 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the creature's spell ends and the arcanaphage feeds.

trait.name: Magic Immunity
trait.text: The arcanaphage is immune to damage from spells. It has advantage on saving throws against all other magical effects.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The arcanaphage makes two tentacle attacks.

action.name: Tentacle
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

reaction.name: Voracious
reaction.text: The arcanaphage's tentacles glow when a spell is cast within 30 feet of it, countering the spell. This reaction works like the counterspell spell, except the arcanaphage must always make a spellcasting ability check, no matter the spell level. Its ability check for this is +5. If it successfully counters the spell, the arcanaphage feeds.

fields.name: Astral Snapper
fields.resist: bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical weapons

trait.name: Astral Devour
trait.text:
A creature hosting an astral snapper's astral form must make a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw each time it finishes a long rest. On a success, the astral snapper is ejected from the host and the Astral Plane into an unoccupied space in the Material Plane within 10 feet of the host and is stunned for 1 round. On a failure, the astral snapper consumes part of the host's internal organs, reducing the host's Constitution score by 1d4. The host dies if this reduces its Constitution to 0. The reduction lasts until the host finishes a long rest after the astral snapper has been expelled. If the host's Constitution score is reduced to 0, the astral snapper exits the host's body in the Material Plane by tearing its way out through the abdomen. The astral snapper becomes completely corporeal as it exits the host, stepping out of the host at its full size.

From the time the astral snapper succeeds on the initial dive into the host through the Astral Plane until the moment it emerges from the host's abdomen, it can be seen by any creature that can see into the Astral Planeits head buried in the host's back. The astral snapper has disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks and is effectively stunned when in this position until it takes damage.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text:
The astral snapper makes two attacks with its claws.

If both attacks hit the same target, the target must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or its wound becomes a rift to the Astral Plane. The astral snapper immediately passes through, closing the rift behind it. The target is then affected by the astral snapper's Astral Devour trait.

action.name: Claws
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) slashing damage.

fields.name: Azeban
fields.skill: Deception +6, Perception +1, Sleight of hand +5, Stealth +5
fields.resist: cold; bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical weapons

trait.name: Elusive
trait.text: The azeban can take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action as a bonus action on each of its turns.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
trait.text: The azeban has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Innate Spellcasting
trait.text:
The azeban's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 14). It can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:

	• At will: dancing lights, disguise self, faerie fire, minor illusion
	• 3/day each: creation, major image, mislead, seeming
	• 1/day each: mirage arcane, programmed illusion

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The azeban makes two attacks. one with its bite and one with its claws.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) piercing damage.

action.name: Claws
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing damage.

action.name: Ear-Splitting Yawp (Recharge 5-6)
action.text: The azeban emits a piercing yell in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 14 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, a target takes 21 (6d6) thunder damage and is deafened for 1 minute. On a success, a creature takes half the damage but isn't deafened. A creature made of inorganic material such as stone, crystal, or metal has disadvantage on this saving throw. A nonmagical object that isn't being worn or carried also takes the damage if it's in the area.

fields.spells: dancing lights, disguise self, faerie fire, minor illusion, creation, major image, mislead, seeming, mirage arcane, programmed illusion

fields.name: Azi Dahaka
fields.resist: cold; bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical weapons

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
trait.text: If Azi Dahaka fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
trait.text: Azi Dahaka has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Multiple Heads
trait.text: Azi Dahaka's three heads grant it advantage on saving throws against being blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, stunned, and knocked unconscious.

trait.name: Reactive Heads
trait.text: Azi Dahaka gets two extra reactions that can be used only for opportunity attacks.

trait.name: Vermin Blood
trait.text: A creature that hits Azi Dahaka with a melee attack while within 5 feet takes 4 (1d8) piercing damage and 4 (1d8) poison damage as the dragon's blood becomes biting and stinging vermin.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: Azi Dahaka makes three bite attacks and two claw attacks.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (1d10 + 5) piercing damage.

action.name: Claw
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) slashing damage.

action.name: Storm Breath (Recharge 56)
action.text: Azi Dahaka exhales a blast of wind and lightning in a 60-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, a target takes 22 (4d10) bludgeoning damage and 18 (4d8) lightning damage, is pushed 25 feet away from Azi Dahaka, and is knocked prone. On a success, a target takes half the bludgeoning and lightning damage and is pushed, but isn't knocked prone. All nonmagical flames in the cone are extinguished.

legendary.name: Legendary Actions (4/Turn)
legendary.text: The dragon can take 4 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The dragon regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

legendary.name: Options
legendary.text: Azi Dahaka can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. Azi Dahaka regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

legendary.name: Control Weather
legendary.text: Azi Dahaka can alter the weather in a 5-mile radius centered on itself. The effect is identical to the control weather spell, except the casting time and effects are immediate.

legendary.name: Call Lightning (Cost 2 Actions)
legendary.text: A bolt of lightning flashes down from the clouds to a point Azi Dahaka can see within 100 feet of it. Each creature within 5 feet of that point must make a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw, taking 16 (3d10) lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

legendary.name: Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary.text:
Azi Dahaka beats its wings.

Each creature within 10 feet of the dragon must succeed on a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw or take 12 (2d6 + 5) bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone. Azi Dahaka can then fly up to half its flying speed.

fields.name: Baba Yaga
fields.resist: cold; bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical weapons

trait.name: Cronesight
trait.text: Baba Yaga has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight. As an action, she can observe a target and magically know its current emotional state. If the target fails a DC 19 Charisma saving throw, she also knows the creature's alignment and discovers a hidden secret about the target.

trait.name: Cronespeech
trait.text: Creatures with Intelligence 3 or lower obey Baba Yaga unquestioningly. Her utterances are often captured as engravings on nearby stone and wood surfaces. These magical reproductions of her words are made in the Common tongue and fade after several days.

trait.name: Grandmother's Teeth
trait.text: The iron teeth of Baba Yaga are sentient, magical, and airborne dentures that sometimes work at cross-purposes to the Old Witch. If the teeth and Baba Yaga are getting along, the teeth reside inside her mouth, providing her with a bite attack and access to its spell list. Baba Yaga can cast a spell from the teeth's innate spell list as a bonus action, using her spellcasting ability. Spells cast in this way are removed from the teeth's spells per day total. If the witch and her teeth are not getting along, the teeth will fly around casting its spells as it wishes (often to the benefit of Baba Yaga's enemies).

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
trait.text: If Baba Yaga fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Mortar And Pestle
trait.text:
Baba Yaga flies in a large mortar and pestle, which is immune to damage and can't be the target of spells or effects. It provides the witch partial cover from ranged attacks.

Baba Yaga doesn't provoke an opportunity attack when she flies out of an enemy's reach. If Baba Yaga is knocked prone, stunned, or incapacitated while flying in the mortar, it will gently set her on the ground and disappear for 1 hour. The pestle remains with the witch.

trait.name: Innate Spellcasting
trait.text:
The baba yaga's innate spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save DC 20, +12 to hit with spell attacks). It can innately cast the following spells, requiring only verbal components:

	• At will: eldritch blast (2d10), message, minor illusion, spare the dying
	• 5/day each: command, disguise self, Tasha's hideous laughter
	• 4/day each: blindness/deafness, darkness, enthrall
	• 3/day each: clairvoyance, counterspell, lightning bolt
	• 2/day each: banishment, blight, polymorph
	• 1/day each: animate objects, insect plague

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: Baba Yaga makes two pestle slap attacks and one bite attack, or three pestle slap attacks.

action.name: Pestle Slap
action.text:
Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 31 (6d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage.

The target must succeed on a DC 20 Constitution saving throw or have disadvantage on concentration checks until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Bite (if iron teeth are equipped)
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 37 (6d10 + 4) piercing damage and the target must succeed on a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened of Baba Yaga until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Breath of the Bone Mother (Recharge 5-6)
action.text: Calling on her elemental powers and her mastery of crone-magic, Baba Yaga exhales a great wind in a 40-foot cone that smells of fetid mires and sausages. Creatures caught in that area must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, a target takes 45 (10d8) necrotic damage and is affected by the bestow curse spell for 1 minute. On a success, a target takes half the necrotic damage but is not cursed. In addition, a creature damaged by the wind releases a stinking cloud (DC 18 Constitution saving throw against the cloud's poison) centered on it at the beginning of its next turn. The cloud dissipates after 1d4 rounds.

reaction.name: Dance of the Time Taunter (1/Day)
reaction.text: When Baba Yaga's turn ends, she can take an additional turn. A creature able to see Baba Yaga dance through time has its understanding of the universe challenged and must succeed on a DC 18 Intelligence saving throw or be stunned until the end of its next turn.

legendary.name: Legendary Actions (4/Turn)
legendary.text: The fey can take 4 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The fey regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

legendary.name: Options
legendary.text: Baba Yaga can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options listed. Only one legendary action can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. She regains spent legendary actions at the start of her turn.

legendary.name: At Will Spell
legendary.text: Baba Yaga casts one at will spell from her list or from her iron teeth's list if it is equipped.

legendary.name: Pestle Slap
legendary.text: Baba Yaga makes one pestle slap attack.

legendary.name: Breath of the Bone Mother (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary.text: Baba Yaga uses Breath of the Bone Mother, if it is available.

Iron's innate spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). It can innately cast the following spells, requiring only verball components:

fields.name: Bar Brawl
fields.resist: piercing, slashing
fields.conditionImmune: charmed, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, prone, restrained, stunned

trait.name: Liquid Courage (Recharge 56)
trait.text: As a bonus action, the bar brawl imbibes nearby alcohol to gain access to a hidden reservoir of audacity and grit. The bar brawl gains 7 (2d6) temporary hp for 1 minute.

trait.name: Swarm
trait.text: The bar brawl can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the bar brawl can move through any opening large enough for a Medium humanoid. Except for Liquid Courage, the bar brawl can't regain hp or gain temporary hp.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The bar brawl makes two melee attacks or two darts attacks.

action.name: Barstool
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 0 ft., one target in the bar brawl's space. 14 (4d6) bludgeoning damage, or 7 (2d6) if the bar brawl has half its hit points or fewer.

action.name: Broken Bottles
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, range 0 ft., one target in the bar brawl's space. 10 (4d4) slashing damage, or 5 (2d4) if the bar brawl has half its hit points or fewer.

action.name: Darts
action.text: Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, range 20/40 ft. 10 (4d4) piercing damage, or 5 (2d4) if the bar brawl has half its hit points or fewer.

fields.name: Barong
fields.resist: bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical weapons

trait.name: Aura of Protection
trait.text: All allies within 30 feet of Barong gain a +6 bonus to saving throws as long as Barong is conscious.

trait.name: Divine Weapons
trait.text: Barong's weapon attacks are magical. When he hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 18 (4d8) radiant damage (already included below).

trait.name: Magic Resistance
trait.text: Barong has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Pack Tactics
trait.text: Barong has advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of his allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: Barong makes two attacks. one with his bite and one with his claws.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +0 to hit, reach 0 ft., plus 18 (4d8 + 0) radiant damage.Melee Weapon Attack: +0 to hit, reach 0 ft., Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit.11 (1d8 + 7) piercing damage

action.name: Claws
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (1d6 + 7) slashing damage plus 18 (4d8) radiant damage.

action.name: Summon Spirit (1/Day)
action.text: Barong can summon any combination of 2d4 good-aligned ghosts, uraeuses (Tome of Beasts p. 392), or couatls; 1d4 temple dogs (Tome of Beasts p. 378), unicorns, or good-aligned wraiths; or one buraq (Tome of Beasts p. 48) or deva. The spirits and celestials appear in unoccupied spaces within 60 feet of Barong and act as his allies. They remain for 1 minute or until Barong dismisses them as an action.

reaction.name: Divine Protection
reaction.text: When a creature makes an attack against Barong or one of his allies within 30 feet, Barong grants the target of the attack a +5 bonus to its AC until the start of his next turn.

legendary.name: Legendary Actions (4/Turn)
legendary.text: The celestial can take 4 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The celestial regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

legendary.name: Options
legendary.text: Barong can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. Barong regains spent legendary actions at the start of his turn.

legendary.name: Claw
legendary.text: Barong makes one claw attack.

legendary.name: Enlightening Roar
legendary.text: Each creature he chooses within 30 feet of him can immediately repeat a saving throw to end one condition currently affecting it.

legendary.name: Divine Command (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary.text: Barong roars a command at one allied undead or celestial within 30 feet of him. It can move up to its speed and make one attack as a reaction. The creature doesn't provoke an opportunity attack from this movement.

fields.name: Giant Albino Bat
fields.languages: Understands Common, Abyssal but can't speak

trait.name: Echolocation
trait.text: The bat can't use its blindsight while deafened.

trait.name: Keen Hearing
trait.text: The bat has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing.

trait.text: The bat can't use its blindsight while deafened.
